newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: Czech PX50 gloom continues, no rebound seen.
newsitem.headline: Czech PX50 gloom continues, no rebound seen.

text.p: The Czech PX50 again failed to post its first upward session in October at Friday's close with dealers saying the downtrend was caused by a combination of declining company profitability and increased political risk.
The PX50 lost 0.5 percent to 542.2 while the major issue dominated RPIX fell 0.4 percent to 1,101.
Most analysts say the situation is unlikely to improve ahead of elections to the newly created Senate in mid-November but some are becoming even more gloomy about company fundamentals.
"I'm afraid its not only a technical correction," said Pavel Sobisek of Zivnostenska Banka in Prague.
"Half year results for companies with more than 100 employees were down about 17 percent in nominal terms compared with same period in 1995 or about 25 percent in real terms," he added.
Sobisek said the decline in company profitability had been evident for a long time.

However, he suggested that the increased political risk in the Czech Republic since the centre-right government lost its parliamentary majority in June's elections had caused analysts to pull back and look at fundamentals more closely.
The conclusions they reached, he said, were now feeding through into lower prices on the bourse.

On the PX50, SPT Telecom was the biggest major issue decliner, losing 21 crowns to 3,210. Komercni Banka fell 10 crowns to 2,205, CEZ was unchanged on 1,013 and Ceska Sporitelna rose six crowns to 325.
Turnover was thin at 569 million crowns.
